correctness_confidence.basis: The universal ordered-layering lower bound, aligned-spike equivalence, one-step interlacing regions, weak-duality obstruction, and exact d=8 rank witness all withstand direct checking. Fresh exact and high-precision reproductions agree with the stated results.

rigor.basis: The all-parameter results are analytic. The computational Theorem 3 uses exact rational primal witnesses and exact Horn/LR identities. Numerical catalogues and conjectures are explicitly segregated from the proved statements.

novelty.basis: The combination of dimension-free ordered-layering certificates, exact interlacing chambers, and an exact lower bound on necessary Horn-box complexity appears original within the checked literature. Exhaustive priority was not established.

significance.basis: The manuscript advances from fixed small inertia to general (m,n), supplies exact full-dimensional regions with optimal rank, and identifies a precise obstruction to the earlier n-1-box expectation.

reproducibility.basis: The bounded revision verifier regenerates Horn lists in memory, and all exact obstructions and the d=8 face certificate replay quickly. Independent supplied theorem tests reran with a cache-free generator and constructed the predicted commutators to near machine precision.

summary: A substantial and well-delimited general-inertia advance. Theorem 1 gives a correct all-(m,n,z) Horn certificate for ordered full-capacity layerings. Theorems 2A and 2B give exact upper constructions on aligned-spike cones and explicit full-dimensional interlacing regions. Theorem 3 rigorously disproves sufficiency of box<=n-1 Horn tiles at (5,4) by an exact weak-duality witness, while the revised d=8 argument exactly certifies rank five. No material objection was found.
strengths: Theorem 1 is genuinely dimension-free and its disjoint-index mechanism explains exactly why full capacity is required.
The path-system characterization gives a concrete structural meaning to diagonal block-shift chains and additive one-spike decompositions.
Theorem 2B uses the inverse rank-one interlacing theorem efficiently and proves nonempty full-dimensional regions with rank-m optimizers.
Theorem 3 excludes every nonnegative certificate from a broad restricted Horn class, rather than merely failing to find one.
The corrected d=8 face argument supplies exact lower inequalities and an exact full-Horn feasible spectrum, closing the rank claim.
The manuscript clearly labels incomplete catalogues, numerical block-size evidence, and general structural conjectures.
weaknesses: The exact regions R_k generally cover only part of the chambers for n>=3; the pure-phase feasibility facets remain unknown.
The broader block-size and finite-form classification in Section 8 is numerical and the sampled reflected catalogue is demonstrably incomplete.
Several motivating comparisons rely on earlier AIRR records that were outside the permitted source set.
